recurrence-coefficient-continuity.scope: All original card conclusions hold for actual positive measures with polynomial moments. Only the first 2n monomial moments need converge, the limiting support may have exactly n points, and early systems may be singular. Finite positive compactly supported measures are included by the existing polynomial-moment integrability theorem.

clauses.statement: Finite moment convergence makes the actual measure Hankel determinants converge and, at the nondegenerate limiting support threshold, makes the approximating Hankel systems eventually positive definite.

Every coefficient of each actual canonical monic measure polynomial through order n converges; every included squared norm and monic alpha/beta recurrence coefficient converges for k<n, including the constant zero beta boundary convention.
Actual measure monic polynomials through order n converge uniformly on every bounded real set and in particular the order-n polynomial converges uniformly on each fixed compact interval [a,b].
The actual normalized measure Jacobi matrices converge in spectral distance, and the actual canonically ordered n-point Gauss nodes and integrated-cardinal weights converge at each index.

recurrence-coefficient-continuity.source: Gautschi (2004), Theorem 2.32 and its corollary; open_mathematical_items_operator_derivations.tex AQ22–AQ23.
recurrence-coefficient-continuity.proof_route: Native measure moments converge in the finite Pi coordinate space. Smooth finite polynomial functionals and exact moment-truncation identities turn the checked canonical data continuity into actual measure convergence. Positive determinant and measure Hankel PSD derive eventual positive definiteness.
recurrence-coefficient-continuity.trust: No new axiom, sorry, native_decide, assumed coefficient/node/weight convergence, or smooth representing-measure family.
recurrence-coefficient-continuity.verification: Direct Lean check and olean export pass without warnings; integrating parent must complete repository-wide checks and atlas synchronization.
